#616 renames this field. Its `m_footprint` emits `shep_install_bytes` (all three binaries) and `shep_archive_gz_bytes` in place of `shep_binary_bytes`, so once both land this reads no shep figure and footprint goes undecided. Switching to `shep_install_bytes` needs a new baseline too: 18811453 in `baseline.json` is one binary, the install is three.

Fixed in 147436e.

- `compare.py` now prefers `shep_install_bytes` and falls back to `shep_binary_bytes`, so it reads either harness.
- The two are different quantities, so every baseline entry now names its `field`. A run carrying the other one is refused with exit 2 and no change printed, rather than read as a 67% win.
- The seed's footprint is now the docs page's own install row, 53.85 MiB, held as `shep_install_bytes`.

#616 landed in the meantime. c1ddb89 merges `main`, and 2040cb6 adds a preflight check that every `[[bin]]` sits beside `SHEP_BIN`. Without it, `m_footprint` only refuses after the whole run, and `--record` then writes nothing.

Tests cover both harness shapes (29 pass). The drift test passes against #616's real `m_footprint` and fails if the harness writes neither field.

An int past float's range makes `math.isfinite` raise `OverflowError`, e.g. `10**400` in a hand-edited `metrics.jsonl`. It escapes `main`, so `record` dies with a traceback and `check` exits 1, the regressed code. Unlikely from the harness, but one `except` closes it:

```suggestion
    try:
        return float(value) if math.isfinite(value) else None
    except OverflowError:
        return None
```

Fixed in f642b8a, with your `except` as suggested. I reproduced it first: a `10**400` round made `check` exit 1 and `record` die with a traceback. With the fix, that round counts as missing and both exit 2.

Because the root cause was "any uncaught error exits 1", `main` now also turns an unexpected exception into exit 2 and prints its traceback. A crash can no longer read as a regression. There are two new tests, one per path; 31 pass.

**Use the `SHEP_BIN` checkout for the footprint manifest.**

`preflight` and `m_footprint` call `shep_bin_names`, which always reads `$SCRATCH/wt-bench/crates/shep-cli/Cargo.toml`. `m_versions` records `HEAD` from the directory containing `SHEP_BIN`. Therefore, an external `SHEP_BIN` can fail preflight when `wt-bench` is absent, or can measure a different `[[bin]]` set when `wt-bench` is at another revision.

Resolve the repository root from `SHEP_BIN` and use its manifest. Keep `wt-bench` as the fallback when `SHEP_BIN` is not inside a checkout.

<details>
<summary>Suggested fix</summary>

```diff
+shep_manifest() {
+  local root
+  root=$(git -C "$(dirname "$SHEP_BIN")" rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null) ||
+    root="$SCRATCH/wt-bench"
+  printf '%s/crates/shep-cli/Cargo.toml\n' "$root"
+}
+
 shep_bin_names() {
   awk '/^\[\[bin\]\]/ { inbin = 1; next }
        /^\[/         { inbin = 0 }
        inbin && /^name = / { gsub(/"/, "", $3); print $3 }' \
-    "$SCRATCH/wt-bench/crates/shep-cli/Cargo.toml"
+    "$(shep_manifest)"
 }
```

</details>

The `--check` path passes `--baseline "$BASELINE"` and all forwarded `compare.py` options. The printed command omits both. Replaying it can use a different baseline and threshold settings, which can produce a different verdict.

<excerpt>Input variables | Release-plz # Input variables The GitHub action accepts the following input variables: - `command`: The release-plz command to run. If unspecified, the `publish` field of the package manifest is used. If the `publish` field is empty, crates.io is used. - `manifest_path`: Path to the Cargo.toml of the project you want to update. <title>release-pr | Release-plz</title>
<location>https://release-plz.dev/docs/usage/release-pr</location>
<excerpt>release-pr | Release-plz # release-pr The `release-plz release-pr` command runs `release-plz update` and opens a GitHub Pull Request that prepares the next release. When the project maintainer merges the release pull request, the packages are ready to be published. Here&`#39`;s an example of a PR opened by release-plz in the release-plz GitHub project itself. In the following example, I run `release-plz` on the `release-plz` project itself. `Release-plz` opens a PR that increases the version and the changelog of the packages with unpublished changes. To learn more, run `release-plz release-pr --help`. ## PR update​ If there&`#39`;s already an open release PR: - If the PR contains commits that are not from bots (except the first one), release-plz closes the PR to preserve the git history. The update mechanism is simple: overwrite everything and force-push. 💥 Reasoning: changes done by bots are not valuable, so we can overwrite them. (Not available on Gitea and GitLab). - Otherwise, release-plz closes the old PR and opens a new one. This is done to preserve the git history of maintainers&`#39`; changes. Release-plz also closes the release PR when it cannot update it (for example, the force-push fails due to merge conflicts). info `release-plz release-pr -p ` doesn&`#39`;t open a PR per package.
